en: So this is the ruin that\nreproduces memories. Truly\nfascinating.
Hm? What is that glowing over\nthere?
Uncle Ernest, wait for me! I\nwant to see too!

Hm, Relia, was it? To have an
interest in ruins at your age
shows great promise. Not bad
at all.

However, for an archaeologist,
fieldwork is essential. You'd
best build up your physical
strength.
Okay, I got it! I'll do my best!

Miss Lilia, if I may offer some
advice, there is no need to
decide on your future dreams
at such a young age.

Many possibilities lie ahead of
you while you are still young. It
won't be too late to think
about your future after you've
explored them.
Uh... ? ...So, um, does that\nmean I shouldn't build up my\nstrength?
Okay, I get it! I'll try lots of\ndifferent things!

M-my apologies, Captain. I
intended to give her advice,
but it seems I've only
succeeded in confusing Miss
Lilia.

So that light from before was
coming from this ore... I'll try a
compositional analysis with the
Quad Scanner.
It's so clear and beautiful... It\nlooks just like the blue sky\nback in Sthal Village.
Oh, look! There's another stone\njust like it over there.
Huh!
Why are the clouds white and\nthe sky blue?
Uh, well...
Why is the soil soft, but stones\nare hard? Please, tell me why!
Fidel and me...? And this is\nSthal Village, right?

Just as I thought. This is a
projection created by an
unknown technology, not a
hologram.
Relia, is this scene from your\nmemories?
Yeah. I remember asking Fidel\nall sorts of questions like that.
But...
...You see, I did something\nmean to Fidel back then.

I just assumed Fidel knew
everything, so I kept asking
"why" and "how" about every
little thing that caught my
interest...

Relia, why are you so down?
Having questions is a good
thing. It creates opportunities
for new learning.
But Fidel looked troubled.

That is also a good thing. Being
troubled means that, until then,
Fidel likely took the blue sky
for granted and never thought
to question it.
The older one gets, the more\nlikely they are to overlook the\nthings they see every day.
You could say that by asking\nthose questions, you gave Fidel\nan opportunity to learn as well.

...Actually, a little while after
Fidel started studying on Earth,
he came to explain to me why
the sky is blue.

I thought he went and looked it
up specifically because I had
asked him so many things back
then.

The fact that he remembered
such a common everyday
conversation suggests that he
was curious about why the sky
is blue himself.
It seems Miss Lilia's questions\nstimulated his intellectual\ncuriosity.
Do you think I was helpful to\nFidel?
Yes, without a doubt.
Then I'll keep asking him things\nI don't understand!
Now, you mustn't only ask\nquestions, Miss Lilia.
Huh?

When you have a doubt, you
must not neglect to think for
yourself, form a hypothesis,
and strive to find the answer.
Hm!?

Hmm, no matter how many
times I see it, it's just so
strange... How can you buy
things when there's nobody
there?
By "buy things," do you mean\nthis vending machine?
Exactly! When E-tan puts\nmoney in here, all sorts of\nthings just come popping out...

This is inside the Cardianon...
This is a memory from shortly
after I first met Mista Edge
and the others.

Oh, I know what that is! It's a
vending machine. I saw them
on Earth. You put money in,
and all kinds of things come
out.
It seems Miss Lilia has fully\nadjusted to life on Earth.
Now, Miss Lilia. Do you know\nhow a vending machine actually\nworks?

Um... you put money in the
machine, and then the item you
chose is... replicated? And then
it comes out.

Now, let us move on to the
mechanism of replication. How
do you think the replication
process occurs?
Hmm... why?

Simply asking questions will not
lead to your own learning. You
must form a hypothesis using
logical thinking.
Log-i-cal... think-ing?

There is no need to overthink
it. Simply use your experiences
and knowledge to imagine, step
by step, how such a thing
could be achieved.
Um...
I bet there's someone inside!\nOr maybe they're using a magic\ncircle to summon the items?
But E-tan isn't using any magic\ncircles... Hmm, it's so\nmysterious!
I think she's heading in the\nwrong direction...

No, taking a different path
toward the answer is not a
waste. What matters is how
one arrives at the conclusion.
B-Bacchus...?
Miss Lymle, your Academic\nThirst is truly wonderful.

I, Bacchus, am deeply
impressed. If you wish, I shall
serve as the guide to lead you
to the answer.

Lymle, you are not only full of
curiosity, but your
determination to face your
questions is also praiseworthy.

Formulating a hypothesis and
then verifying it. That is a
rational way of thinking. The
fact that she doesn't simply
ask her companions for the
answer suggests she is
well-suited to be a scholar.

Yes, I believe Lymle possesses
such great power as a caster
not only because of her
aptitude, but also because of
her personality.

Miss Lilia, I suggest you also
try forming a hypothesis
regarding your own questions.
If you wish, I shall be your
guide.
Hmm...
You look quite dissatisfied.
...C-could it be that I am\ninsufficient as a guide?
Uncle Bacchus, why is it that\nyou usually call Lymle "Lymle,"\nbut you call me "Miss Lilia"?
T-that is...
No, that's not it!
Not it...? Do you mean you\nhave already reached the\nanswer on your own?
Geez, Lym doesn't know\nanything about "Miss." Lym is\nLymle!
I'm not "Miss Lilia" either, I'm\njust Relia. I want you to call me\nRelia.
Now, now, Miss Lilia. I believe\naddressing someone without a\ntitle would be rude.

My teacher on Earth said that
remembering each other's
names and calling each other
by them is the first step to
becoming close.
I know the true meaning of\nthose words.
When I first met Fidel and Miki,\nthey called my name so many\ntimes.
It made me happy. By calling\nmy name, they gave me a\nplace where I belong.
But the way you call me, Uncle\nBacchus, feels a little lonely... It\nmakes you feel far away.
...No, that wasn't my intention...

I want to get closer to you,
Uncle Bacchus, as we continue
our journey. I want to talk
about all sorts of things.
So, I want you to call me Relia!
Hmm, a coherent argument\nbased on both personal\nexperience and knowledge.

Bacchus. It seems Relia
possesses a capacity for
logical thinking, even without
your instruction.
Miss Re... no, Relia. Your point\nis well taken. Very well. I shall\ncall you Relia from now on.
Yeah, thank you!
Now, back to the topic.\nRegarding the mechanism of\nthe Replicate...
I think that conversation can\nwait until we return to the ship.
For now, exploring these ruins\ntakes priority.

Ruins that project human
memories... In other words, I
believe it accesses the brains
of the people
inside―specifically the cerebral
cortex―to reproduce them.
Does that mean these ruins\ncan peek inside my head?!

That part isn't particularly
difficult. Technology to analyze
brain signals to read emotions
or create imagery has existed
for hundreds of years.
However, Mr. Fayt mentioned\nthat events he had no memory\nof were played back.

You mean the story where
Grandpa Adray told Fayt he
should definitely make Clair his
bride.
But Fayt, Grandpa Adray, and\nClair all said they had\nabsolutely no memory of that.
That is an interesting\nphenomenon. In that case,\nperhaps it is reading desires...

Though, it is unlikely that
something without a clear form,
like a desire, could create such
a vivid image.
If that's the case, the only\npossibility is...
This must be that logical\nthinking Uncle Bacchus was\ntalking about.

Indeed. It is a vital way of
thinking for those in
professions like Mista Ernest's,
who must constantly face the
unknown.
...Could we assume that these\nruins aren't actually extracting\ninformation from our brains?

...I recall a lecture at the
university in Princebridge that
discussed the causal
determination of uncertain
events.

I can't exactly go back and
attend the lectures at Energy
Nede again, but it might be
worth searching for similar
literature...
Hm!
Yo, Claude. What brings you to\nthis sacred hall of learning?
Oh, it's nothing in particular,\nreally...

Well, it's good that you came
regardless. There is an infinite
amount of knowledge here for
us to learn.
Everyone seems to be listening\nto the lecture so quietly.
That's because it's currently\nexam season.

Is this a memory of when I was
attending lectures at the
university in Princebridge on
Energy Nede...?

Mista Ernest and his
companions have visited
Energy Nede before, haven't
they?
That's right. To you Morphus,\nthey were former comrades\nwho went their separate ways.
Indeed. Seeing them study so\ndesperately reminds me of my\nstudent days at EnII... hm?

It looks like everyone is writing
things on small scraps of
paper instead of in their
notebooks. I wonder what
they're doing?

That's called cheating. During
the exam, they pull out those
little slips of paper and copy
the answers onto their sheets.
What?! Is that actually\nallowed!?
Of course it isn't!! Mista Ernest,\nwhat on earth are you teaching\na child!!

An exam is meant to be a
place to demonstrate the
results of one's daily studies. If
you listen to the lectures
seriously, there is no need for
such things.
Seriously, huh? A safe\nanswer, but it lacks flair.
Why you...!
Listen. An exam is a serious\nbattle of wits between the\nproctor and the student.
The student tries to cheat\nwithout getting caught, and the\nproctor tries to find them.
It's a battle where both sides\nput their heart and soul on the\nline.
Right...
Bacchus, you use that body of\nyours to look things up, don't\nyou?
I do, but... what does that have\nto do with any of this?!
There's no need to memorize\nknowledge. When you need it,\nyou just look it up then.
Just like you do, Bacchus.

That is completely different
from taking an exam! In the
first place, the purpose of an
exam is...
Um, I think it's like this.

Even if you try to remember
everything from class, it's hard
to get it all perfectly. That's
why the teacher said we write
things in our notebooks to read
them over.

But if you forget the lesson
entirely, you won't even know
where to start reading in your
notebook.

I bet it's really hard to
remember everything, even on
Earth or other planets with
amazing technology.

But if you remember the basics
from the exam, you can recall
them and look up the details
whenever you want to know
more.
So, you're saying it's necessary\nto take exams seriously?
Yeah. I mean, if you hadn't paid\nattention to your lectures at\nEnergy Nede, Uncle Ernest...

...you wouldn't have
remembered the lecture that
might help solve the mystery
of these ruins, right?

Knowledge to help you search
for more knowledge, and
knowledge to connect different
pieces of information. Lectures
and exams exist so that one
may acquire these things.

And the people taking notes on
those tiny scraps of paper
might be doing it so they can
pull them out and read them
faster than a notebook.

...To think I'd be outdone by
such a young child. A
fascinating experience indeed.
I've learned something today.

This story has come to an end.
More stories will be released in
the future. Please look forward
to them.
